added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and every integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A,
 \qquad Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k.
\]
These identities require only finite moments through order \(k\), source independence, and the maintained latent-profile plane; no global moment generating function is used.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), an environment \(e\), and an integer \(k\geq2\).  The all-orders moment condition in the definition of \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) implies that every product moment occurring below is finite.  For random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\), the joint cumulant is the finite moment--cumulant polynomial
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_k}
 (|\pi|-1)!(-1)^{|\pi|-1}
 \prod_{D\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right],
 \tag{1}
\]
where \(\mathfrak P_k\) is the set of partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).  Each variable occurs exactly once in each monomial in (1), so (1) is linear in each argument.  If the arguments can be split into two nonempty independent groups, substitution of the corresponding factorization of every block moment into (1) gives zero.  Equivalently, in the truncated formal moment series the coefficient in (1) is the coefficient of the corresponding monomial in the formal logarithm; independence factors the moment series, and
\(\log(M_1M_2)=\log M_1+\log M_2\) has no monomial involving variables from both groups.  This argument is purely polynomial through total degree \(k\) and does not require an analytic moment generating function.

The structural equations give
\[
 T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad
 Y_e=\beta T_e+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{2}
\]
Apply separate linearity of (1) to the mixed cumulant with one \(Y_e\) argument and \(k-1\) copies of \(T_e\).  Because \(\epsilon_y\) is independent of \((U_e,\epsilon_{t,e})\), and hence of \(T_e\), the independent-groups consequence of (1) makes its term vanish.  Therefore
\[
 \kappa_k(Y_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 =\beta\kappa_k(T_e)+
   \gamma\kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e).
 \tag{3}
\]
Expanding the last \(k-1\) arguments by the first equation in (2), every term containing both \(U_e\) and \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) vanishes by their independence.  The only surviving term is the all-\(U_e\) term, and thus
\[
 \kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 =\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(U_e)
 =\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(\epsilon_{u,e}).
 \tag{4}
\]
Combining (3)--(4) and subtracting the corresponding equality for the reference environment \(0\), the definitions of \(m_k,c_k,u_k\) yield, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 m_k=\beta c_k+\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k.
 \tag{5}
\]
The latent-profile condition in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) gives \(u_k\in A\), and scalar multiplication preserves membership in a linear subspace.  Hence the second term on the right of (5) belongs to \(A\).  Since \(Q_A\) is the orthogonal-complement projector, \(Q_Au_k=0\).  Applying \(Q_A\) to (5) proves
\[
 Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k,
\]
as asserted.

added_lemmas.statement:
The structural direct effect \(\beta\) is point-identified relative to \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) at every parameter with \(r^\star<\infty\), without requiring \(r^\star\leq R_{\max}\).  More precisely, for every integer \(k\geq d+2\) such that \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\),
\[
 \beta=
 \frac{\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle}
      {\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2}.
\]
On the bounded legal-swap domain \(\mathcal D_\rho\), \(\beta\) is identified if and only if \(r^\star<\infty\).  Indeed, every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\) and \(S\theta\) induce the same collection \(\{P_e:e\in\mathcal E\}\), both belong to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), and their effects are the distinct numbers \(\beta\) and \(\beta+\gamma/\alpha\).  The positive result is a statement about the new low-rank population flag class, not about arbitrary simultaneous source shifts.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The causal target is the coefficient \(\beta\), rather than a definition made from observed cumulants.  Under an intervention setting treatment to \(t\), while holding the exogenous variables fixed, the outcome equation becomes
\[
 Y_e(t)=\beta t+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus replacing \(t\) by \(t+1\) changes the potential outcome by \(\beta\); this establishes the causal meaning of the target independently of the observable functional below.

Let \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and suppose \(r^\star<\infty\).  By the definition of the first breakout, there is an integer \(k\geq d+2\) for which \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\).  The population cumulant-cancellation lemma gives
\[
 Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k.
 \tag{7}
\]
Taking the Euclidean inner product of (7) with \(Q_Ac_k\) gives
\[
 \langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle
 =\beta\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2.
 \tag{8}
\]
The denominator in (8) is strictly positive because \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\), so division is valid and yields the displayed quotient.

Every object on the right side is determined by the observed laws.  Specifically, the finite moments guaranteed by \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) determine the cumulants and hence \(c_k,m_k\); the observed contrasts \(c_2,\ldots,c_{d+1}\) determine \(C\); the rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\) makes \(C^\top C\) invertible; and the projector definition then determines \(Q_A\).  Now let \(\widetilde\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) induce the same collection of observed laws as \(\theta\).  It has the same \(c_j,m_j,C,Q_A\) for every \(j\), so it has the same finite \(r^\star\).  Applying (8) to \(\widetilde\theta\) gives
\[
 \widetilde\beta
 =\frac{\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle}
        {\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2}
 =\beta.
\]
This proves point identification relative to the broad population class.  No order cap was used.

We next restrict attention to \(\mathcal D_\rho\).  The definition of the bounded ambient class makes \(\Theta\subseteq\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  Hence every \(\theta\in\mathcal B\), for which \(d+2\leq r^\star\leq R_{\max}\), is covered by the preceding identification argument, even against every observationally equivalent alternative in the larger class \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\).

Let instead \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\).  The treatment-loading bound gives \(|\alpha|\geq a_0>0\), so define
\[
 V_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},
 \qquad W_e=\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad q=\frac{\gamma}{\alpha}.
\]
The structural equations then read
\[
 T_e=V_e+W_e,
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{9}
\]
Under the source swap, the latent and treatment sources are respectively \(W_e\) and \(V_e\), while the coefficients are \(1,\beta+q,-q\).  Consequently its observables satisfy
\[
 T'_e=W_e+V_e=T_e,
\]
and
\[
 Y'_e=(\beta+q)(W_e+V_e)-qW_e+\epsilon_y
      =(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y=Y_e.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus the swap preserves the complete observed law in every environment, not merely the displayed cumulants.

By definition of \(\mathcal N_\rho\), both \(\theta\) and \(S\theta\) are in \(\Theta_\rho^\circ\) and both have infinite breakout.  To verify that the alternative itself belongs to \(\mathcal N_\rho\), compute
\[
 S^2\theta=
 \left(1,\beta,\frac{\gamma}{\alpha},
       \{\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e}\}_{e\in\mathcal E},
       \epsilon_y\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
The loading \(1\) is interior because it is already the loading of \(S\theta\); the effect \(\beta\) and confounding ratio \(\gamma/\alpha\) inherit the interior bounds of \(\theta\).  The two source families in (11) are the two source families of \(S\theta\) in reverse order, so centeredness, mutual independence, all-order moment existence, and the finite moment envelope are inherited from \(S\theta\).  The latent shift at order \(k\) in (11) is \(\alpha^ku_k\), which belongs to \(A\) because \(u_k\in A\).  Equations (9)--(10), applied once more, show that its observed laws, calibration matrix, calibration gap, and infinite breakout equal those of \(\theta\).  Hence \(S^2\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\) and \(r^\star(S^2\theta)=\infty\).  The definition of the no-breakout branch now gives
\[
 S\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\subseteq\mathcal D_\rho.
\]

Finally, the two effects differ by \(q=\gamma/\alpha\).  The confounding bound gives \(|q|\geq q_0>0\), so they are distinct.  Since two parameters in \(\mathcal D_\rho\) with the same observed laws have different causal targets, no observed-law functional identifies \(\beta\) at a point of \(\mathcal N_\rho\).  Since \(\mathcal D_\rho=\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N_\rho\), identification holds there exactly on the finite-breakout branch.  The broad positive result used only membership in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), whereas the negative result used the explicit bounded legal-swap restriction; this proves the two scopes stated in the theorem.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem separates unrestricted-order population identification from bounded inference and legal-swap nonidentification: any finite orthogonal cumulant flag identifies the structural effect in the new low-rank population class.
added_lemmas.gap: Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, gives a simultaneous-shift obstruction in a two-environment setting. It does not provide the projected-plane recovery map or identification at an arbitrary finite breakout in this new calibrated multi-environment submodel.
added_lemmas.consumer: For a selected edge in the Sachs perturbation panel, the theorem returns a direct-effect functional whenever the maintained population profile has a finite flag, while the bounded no-breakout branch reports an exact source-label ambiguity.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(d=1\), \(E=3\), and an integer \(r\) with \(3\leq r\leq R_{\max}\).  There exist compatible interior bounds and centered independent compound-Poisson source families for which, with
\[
 a=(1,2)^\top,
 \qquad b=(2,-1)^\top,
\]
the latent cumulant-shift profile is a positive multiple of \(a\), while the treatment-noise profile is a positive multiple of \(a\) plus a binomial finite-difference perturbation in direction \(b\) that vanishes below order \(r\) and equals a nonzero multiple of \(r!b\) at order \(r\).  Both source laws change in every pair of environments.  For each environment pair the scalar calibration contrast is nonzero and the legal source swap gives an observationally equivalent, unequal-effect, no-breakout representation.  Jointly, the original parameter has \(r^\star=r\) and is identified, whereas the swapped latent profile leaves the maintained one-dimensional plane at order \(r\), so the pairwise swap is not a legal joint alternative.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\in\{3,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and write
\[
 a_0=b_0=0,
 \qquad (a_1,a_2)=(1,2),
 \qquad (b_1,b_2)=(2,-1).
\]
For \(1\leq j\leq r\), put
\[
 \nu_{rj}=(-1)^{r-j}\binom rj,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{r,k}=\sum_{j=1}^r\nu_{rj}j^k.
\]
The binomial identity
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^{r-j}\binom rj e^{jt}=(e^t-1)^r
 \tag{12}
\]
and differentiation at \(t=0\) give
\[
 \Delta_{r,k}=0\quad(1\leq k<r),
 \qquad
 \Delta_{r,r}=r!.
 \tag{13}
\]

Choose \(\eta,\zeta,\varepsilon,L_u,L_t>0\) with
\[
 L_t>2\varepsilon\max_{1\leq j\leq r}|\nu_{rj}|.
 \tag{14}
\]
For each \(e\in\{0,1,2\}\), let \(N^u_e\) be Poisson with intensity
\(L_u+\eta a_e\), and set
\[
 \epsilon_{u,e}=N^u_e-(L_u+\eta a_e).
\]
For the treatment source, take independent Poisson variables \(N^t_{e,j}\) with intensities
\[
 \lambda^t_{e,j}=L_t+\zeta a_e\mathbf 1\{j=1\}
                    +\varepsilon b_e\nu_{rj},
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq r,
 \tag{15}
\]
and set
\[
 \epsilon_{t,e}=\sum_{j=1}^rj(N^t_{e,j}-\lambda^t_{e,j}).
\]
Inequality (14), together with \(|b_e|\leq2\), makes every intensity in (15) strictly positive.  Take an independent centered Gaussian \(\epsilon_y\), and make all sources mutually independent within each environment.  Centering is explicit.  Because the jumps are bounded and the Poisson intensities are finite, each source has finite absolute moments of every integer order; in fact its moment generating function is finite for every real argument.

For a centered compound-Poisson sum with jump sizes \(j\) and intensities \(\lambda_j\), direct differentiation of
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp\!\left{t\sum_jj(N_j-\lambda_j)\right}
 =\sum_j\lambda_j(e^{jt}-1-jt)
 \tag{16}
\]
shows that its cumulant of every order \(k\geq2\) is \(\sum_j\lambda_jj^k\).  Hence the two environmental source profiles, relative to environment \(0\), are
\[
 u_k=\eta a,
 \qquad
 w_k:=
 \bigl(\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e})-
       \kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,0})\bigr)_{e=1}^2
 =\zeta a+\varepsilon\Delta_{r,k}b.
 \tag{17}
\]
Both source families change in every environment pair: the coordinates \(a_0,a_1,a_2\) are pairwise distinct, and, by (13), the treatment-source second-cumulant difference between environments \(e\) and \(f\) is \(\zeta(a_e-a_f)\neq0\).

Set
\[
 \alpha=1,
 \qquad \beta=-q/2,
 \qquad \gamma=q,
 \tag{18}
\]
where \(q>0\).  By source independence and cumulant additivity, (17) gives
\[
 c_k=u_k+w_k
     =(\eta+\zeta)a+\varepsilon\Delta_{r,k}b.
 \tag{19}
\]
Since \(r\geq3\), equations (13) and (19) imply
\[
 C=[c_2]=[(\eta+\zeta)a],
 \qquad
 A=\operatorname{span}\{a\}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The calibration vector is nonzero.  Moreover,
\(a^\top b=1\cdot2+2\cdot(-1)=0\), so (13), (19), and the orthogonal-projector definition yield
\[
 Q_Ac_k=0\quad(3\leq k<r),
 \qquad
 Q_Ac_r=\varepsilon r!b\neq0.
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus the original joint parameter has \(r^\star=r\).  Its latent profiles \(u_k=\eta a\) lie in \(A\) at every order, so the population identification theorem applies and identifies the structural effect \(-q/2\) from the joint laws.

Now choose the fixed coefficient bounds so that
\[
 a_0+\rho<1<a_1-\rho,
 \qquad
 q_0+\rho<q<q_1-\rho,
 \qquad
 q/2<B-\rho.
 \tag{22}
\]
Choose \(\kappa_0>0\) with
\[
 \kappa_0+\rho<(\eta+\zeta)
 \min_{e\neq f}|a_e-a_f|=\eta+\zeta,
 \tag{23}
\]
and choose \(M\) above the maximum \((2R_{\max}+\delta)\)-moment of the finitely many source variables in the construction and their swapped versions, with margin \(\rho\).  Such an \(M\) is finite by (16).  These choices make the original and swapped coefficients and sources interior whenever they are restricted to any two environments.

Indeed, for a pair \(e\neq f\), the one-dimensional observed calibration contrast is
\[
 c_2^{ef}=(\eta+\zeta)(a_e-a_f)\neq0.
 \tag{24}
\]
It has magnitude at least \(\eta+\zeta>\kappa_0+\rho\), so it has rank one and its column space is all of \(\mathbb R\).  Consequently its orthogonal projector is zero and every order is pairwise no-breakout, for both source labelings.  The source-swap algebra gives, within that pair,
\[
 T'_e=T_e,
 \qquad Y'_e=Y_e,
 \qquad
 \beta'=-q/2+q=q/2.
 \tag{25}
\]
Equations (22)--(24) and the choice of \(M\) make both pairwise representations legal members of the corresponding swap-safe interior.  Their effects differ by \(q>0\).

Joint legality fails for the swapped representation for a precise reason.  Under the swap its latent source is the original treatment source, whose order-\(r\) profile is, by (13) and (17),
\[
 w_r=\zeta a+\varepsilon r!b.
\]
Because \(b\neq0\) and \(b\perp a\), this vector does not belong to \(A=\operatorname{span}\{a\}\).  The swapped joint parameter therefore violates the latent-profile-plane condition and is not in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), although every one-dimensional pairwise restriction satisfies that condition automatically.  This proves simultaneous pairwise ambiguity and joint three-environment rescue.
added_lemmas.justification: The construction is the explicit joint-rescue certificate: all three environment pairs retain a legal unequal-effect source ambiguity, but the joint orthogonal direction identifies the effect.
added_lemmas.gap: It establishes only the demonstrated intersection with the two-environment obstruction, and does not claim that the new low-rank class contains every simultaneous-shift model considered by Kivva et al.
added_lemmas.consumer: It explains why three suitably heterogeneous protein-signaling environments can carry identifying geometry that is absent from every pairwise reduction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The broad population class imposes no coefficient envelope; the existing effect-bound assumption continues to restrict beta on the bounded inference and legal-swap subclass.

proposed_core_edits.name: \Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}
proposed_core_edits.reason: Names the broad population identification class separately from the bounded inference and legal-swap class.

novel.justification: Finite absolute moments of every integer order are the maintained requirement actually used for population cumulants. A positive-radius analytic moment generating function, including the local condition used by Kivva et al., implies this condition, while global finiteness on the whole real line is unnecessary.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The cumulant proofs use only finite moment-cumulant polynomials order by order; global real-mgf finiteness was an unused strengthening.

proposed.name: population cumulant-flag class
proposed.construction:
Let \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) be the class of parameters
\[
 \theta=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,
          \{\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e}\}_{e\in\mathcal E},
          \epsilon_y)
\]
for which \(U_e=\epsilon_{u,e}\),
\(T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e}\), and
\(Y_e=\beta T_e+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y\) for every
\(e\in\mathcal E\), and which satisfy every member property listed below.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the broad population class needed for arbitrary finite-order identification, with only structural equations, source independence, all required moments, calibration rank, and the latent profile plane.

proposed.name: bounded calibrated simultaneous-shift model
proposed.construction:
Set
\[
 \Theta=\{\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}:
 \theta\text{ satisfies every bounded-model member property listed below}\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Makes the bounded model explicitly a subclass of the broad population flag class and reserves its additional coefficient, finite-envelope, order-cap, centering, and gap restrictions for inference and legal swaps.
The replacement proves the same cancellation identity on the broader population class directly from the finite moment-cumulant polynomial, so the bounded-class version is obsolete.
The replacement separates broad arbitrary-order population identification from the bounded-domain if-and-only-if legal-swap frontier, as required by the strengthened scope.

prose_updates.tldr: In a new low-rank population submodel of simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts, any finite projected cumulant breakout identifies the structural effect, even above the inference order cap, while the bounded no-breakout branch retains an exact legal source-label ambiguity. A three-environment construction shows that every pair can remain source-swap ambiguous although the joint orthogonal flag identifies. On each first-breakout shell of every fixed admissible bounded model, the theory gives estimator-risk and conservative expected-length upper bounds; conservative coverage and asymptotically exact externally randomized calibration extend over the whole bounded class. Matching minimax lower bounds are established on one fixed compatible experiment.

project_justification.gap: The closest higher-moment result of Kivva et al. establishes a simultaneous-shift obstruction in a two-environment setting. It does not identify effects in arbitrary simultaneous-shift models, and its obstruction transfers here only on the explicitly constructed pairwise intersection. Covariance-based multi-environment methods impose different diagonal-shift geometry and do not supply the treatment-versus-latent source-label frontier studied here.
project_justification.niche: A newly imposed rank-\(d\) latent cumulant-profile plane creates a joint environmental direction that can be invisible in every pairwise reduction. Its first orthogonal breakout separates broad population identification from exact bounded-class source ambiguity and also serves as the statistical strength parameter.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an explicit observed-law quotient for every finite breakout in the broad all-orders population flag class, a legal-swap if-and-only-if frontier on the bounded domain, and a compound-Poisson \(d=1,E=3\) witness with pairwise ambiguity but joint rescue. It also gives the sharp environment and moment-order constructions, estimator and conservative interval upper bounds for every fixed admissible bounded model, matching lower bounds on one fixed compatible experiment, a uniform same-sample generated-projector expansion, and an externally randomized Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin calibration valid through singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.

prose_updates.related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap argument, provide the closest two-environment simultaneous-shift obstruction and motivate the pairwise comparison. Their positive-radius local analytic moment condition implies the all-integer-order moment condition maintained here; global real-mgf finiteness is not needed. The present result concerns a new calibrated low-rank multi-environment submodel and does not claim positive identification for arbitrary simultaneous shifts in their published class. The obstruction is asserted to transfer only on the explicit pairwise intersection certified by the three-environment construction. Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) give BACKSHIFT's contrasting covariance joint-diagonalization condition, not the present profile, rank, or gap restrictions. Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) study higher-cumulant recovery under other latent, intervention, proxy, or instrumental structures. Long et al. (2023) provide an environmental GMM template, while Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) concern singularity-robust testing for supplied moments rather than the present generated cumulant plane. Davis and Kahan (1970) support spectral-projector perturbation only. Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) document complications in the Sachs setting, and Sachs et al. (2005) supply the multi-perturbation application rather than evidence that the new profile condition holds.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The statistical results remain fixed-dimensional and use the bounded subclass's \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) envelope, balanced shares, fixed calibration gap, and fixed order cap. The deterministic Anderson--Rubin interval is conservative over every fixed admissible bounded \(\Theta\). The covariance-adaptive refinement is asymptotic and its exact coverage is unconditional over the data and all external Gaussian and Monte Carlo draws; it does not promise finite-sample exactness, conditional-on-randomization coverage, or deterministic threshold calibration at an atom. Matching full-observation minimax lower bounds are proved only on one fixed compatible experiment. No expected-length or diameter optimality is claimed for \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: Population identification is proved only in the new all-orders low-rank flag class \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), not for arbitrary simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts. The if-and-only-if statement is confined to the bounded legal-swap union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), whose no-breakout branch requires both source labelings to remain interior. The three-environment witness shows a genuine pairwise intersection with the Kivva et al. obstruction, but does not embed their whole published class. The explicit no-breakout and lower-bound constructions require compatible choices of coefficient, moment, and singular-gap bounds. A finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) cannot certify global no-breakout, although any later finite population breakout remains identifying. Estimator-risk and conservative expected-length upper bounds are universal over each fixed admissible bounded \(\Theta\), whereas matching minimax lower bounds are established only on one fixed compatible experiment. The randomized-jitter interval has asymptotically exact unconditional coverage over the bounded class, including no-breakout laws, but no expected-length or diameter optimality claim. The Sachs data motivate the consumer and do not verify the profile restriction.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem quantifies the statistical boundary near a finite flag: estimator risk and conservative interval length are shell-specific, while conservative coverage extends across every fixed admissible bounded model.
statement_notes.gap: Environmental GMM and generic Anderson--Rubin methods do not derive this structural weak-flag rate with a same-sample estimated cumulant plane. The matching lower bound is certified on one fixed compatible experiment, not on every arbitrary nonempty shell.
statement_notes.consumer: The result converts a protein-signaling flag magnitude into a precision and consistency diagnostic while retaining conservative coverage when no flag is present.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every triangular array \((\theta_n)\) with \(\theta_n\in\Theta\), sampled according to the declared independent stratified sampling model, write the observation in environment \(e\) as \(W_{e,i}=(T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})\), put \(C^+=(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top\), and put \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\).  There are centered first-projection arrays \(\psi^C_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\), \(\psi^c_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})\), and \(\psi^m_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})\) such that, simultaneously for \(d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)
 =Z_{n,k}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 Z_{n,k}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i}),
\]
uniformly over all such arrays, where
\[
 \zeta_{e,k,n}
 =Q_A\bigl(\psi^m_{e,k,n}-\beta\psi^c_{e,k,n}
       -\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\bigr).
\]
The remainder is uniform in probability, and the stacked vector \(Z_n=(Z_{n,k}:d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max})\) satisfies
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_n=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\pi_e^{-1}
 \mathbb E\bigl[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}\bigr],
\]
uniformly over the bounded ambient class.  This conclusion allows \(\Sigma_n\) to be singular; \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\) is then the Gaussian law supported on \(\operatorname{im}(\Sigma_n)\).  The term \(-Q_A\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\) is the same-sample estimated-\(A\) correction.  No breakout, first-breakout order, or lower bound on \(\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2\) is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary triangular array \((\theta_n)\) in \(\Theta\).  All constants below depend only on the fixed bounds defining \(\Theta\), the balanced-share constants, \(E\), \(d\), and \(R_{\max}\), and hence are uniform over this array.  The declared sampling model gives independence within and across environments and identical distribution with law \(P_e\) within environment \(e\).  By the balanced-share assumption,
\[
 n_e=n\pi_e\geq n\underline\pi . \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\) in every environment for all sufficiently large \(n\), and the small-sample fallback in the cumulant-SVD definition is eventually inactive.

Set \(s_0=2R_{\max}+\delta\).  The effect, treatment-loading, and confounding bounds imply
\[
 |\alpha|\leq a_1,
 \qquad |\beta|\leq B,
 \qquad |\gamma|=|\alpha|\,|\gamma/\alpha|\leq a_1q_1. \tag{2}
\]
The structural equations in the ambient-class definition give
\[
 T_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e}+\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\beta\alpha+\gamma)\epsilon_{u,e}
      +\beta\epsilon_{t,e}+\epsilon_y. \tag{3}
\]
For \(s_0>1\), convexity gives
\[
 |x_1+\cdots+x_j|^{s_0}
 \leq j^{s_0-1}\sum_{a=1}^j|x_a|^{s_0}. \tag{4}
\]
Applying (4) to (3), then using (2) and the source moment-envelope assumption, yields a constant \(K_W<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_n\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \mathbb E_{\theta_n}\|W_{e,1}\|^{2R_{\max}+\delta}
 \leq K_W. \tag{5}
\]
Every moment and cumulant of \((T_e,Y_e)\) through order \(R_{\max}\) is therefore uniformly bounded.  In particular, the finite dimension of the contrast vectors gives uniform bounds on \(C\), \(c_k\), \(m_k\), and \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\) for \(2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\).

We next derive the influence representations.  For variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\), the moment--cumulant polynomial is
\[
 \kappa_k(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\mathcal P\in\Pi_k}
 (|\mathcal P|-1)!(-1)^{|\mathcal P|-1}
 \prod_{D\in\mathcal P}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right], \tag{6}
\]
where \(\Pi_k\) is the finite set of partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).  For a partition with \(s\) blocks, average the corresponding block monomials over \(s\) distinct observations and symmetrize.  Its expectation is the product in (6), so the unbiased sample cumulant stipulated in the estimator definition is a fixed finite linear combination of symmetric \(U\)-statistics of orders at most \(k\), with kernels of total degree at most \(k\).

Consider one order-\(s\) constituent \(U_{n_e,s}(g)\).  Successively subtracting conditional expectations produces canonical projections \(g_j\), \(1\leq j\leq s\), and the exact identity
\[
 U_{n_e,s}(g)-\mathbb Eg
 =\frac1{n_e}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\psi_g(W_{e,i})
  +\sum_{j=2}^s {s\choose j}U_{n_e,j}(g_j), \tag{7}
\]
where
\[
 \psi_g(w)=s\{\mathbb E[g(w,W_2,\ldots,W_s)]-\mathbb Eg\}.
\]
Each \(g_j\) is centered conditionally on any one argument.  In the second moment of \(U_{n_e,j}(g_j)\), two distinct index sets have zero cross expectation whenever their union contains an index belonging to only one set; if the sets are distinct, such an index exists.  Hence only equal index sets contribute and
\[
 \mathbb E\{U_{n_e,j}(g_j)^2\}
 ={n_e\choose j}^{-1}\mathbb E(g_j^2)
 \leq K n_e^{-j}. \tag{8}
\]
The final inequality is uniform because the squared kernels have degree at most \(2R_{\max}\), and (5), conditional Jensen's inequality, and H\"older's inequality bound all their second moments.  Since the numbers of orders, partitions, environments, and coordinates are fixed, the sum of the terms in (7) having projection order at least two is \(O_{L^2}(n_e^{-1})\), uniformly.

Apply the environment-versus-baseline signs in the contrast definitions and stack the corresponding first projections.  This defines centered arrays \(\psi^C_{e,n}\), \(\psi^c_{e,k,n}\), and \(\psi^m_{e,k,n}\).  Equations (1), (7), and (8) give, simultaneously over the finitely many relevant \(k\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(\widehat C-C)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^C_{e,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1),\\
 \sqrt n(\widehat c_k-c_k)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^c_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1),\\
 \sqrt n(\widehat m_k-m_k)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^m_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1).
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Here uniform \(o_{L^2}(1)\) follows because multiplication of the bound \(O_{L^2}(n_e^{-1})\) by \(\sqrt n\) gives \(O(n^{-1/2})\) under (1).

Put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\}>0. \tag{10}
\]
Each first projection in (9) is a finite sum of polynomials of degree at most \(R_{\max}\) in one observation, with coefficients given by uniformly bounded lower-order moments.  Conditional Jensen's inequality and (5) therefore give
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta_n}\mathbb E_{\theta_n}\!\left[
 \|\psi^C_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}
 +\sum_{k=2}^{R_{\max}}
 \{\|\psi^c_{e,k,n}\|^{2+\nu}
   +\|\psi^m_{e,k,n}\|^{2+\nu}\}
 \right]<\infty, \tag{11}
\]
because \((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\).

We now linearize the generated projector.  Let \(P_C=CC^+\), where \(C^+=(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top\); then \(Q_A=I_{E-1}-P_C\).  The calibration-rank and calibration-gap assumptions license the inverse and imply
\[
 \|C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_d(C)^{-1}\leq\kappa_0^{-1}. \tag{12}
\]
For a perturbation \(H\) with \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0/2\), the triangle inequality gives \(\sigma_d(C+H)\geq\kappa_0/2\).  With \(G=C^\top C\) and \(D=C^\top H+H^\top C+H^\top H\), the exact inverse identity
\[
 (G+D)^{-1}=G^{-1}-G^{-1}DG^{-1}
 +G^{-1}DG^{-1}D(G+D)^{-1} \tag{13}
\]
can be substituted into the formula for \(P_{C+H}\).  Collecting the linear terms and bounding every remaining product by (5), (12), and \(\sigma_d(C+H)\geq\kappa_0/2\) gives
\[
 P_{C+H}-P_C
 =Q_AHC^+ +(Q_AHC^+)^\top+R_C(H),
 \qquad \|R_C(H)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq K_P\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2, \tag{14}
\]
with \(K_P\) uniform.

Equation (9) and (11) imply \(\|\widehat C-C\|=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  Taking \(H=\widehat C-C\) in (14), the event on which (14) applies has probability tending to one uniformly, and its remainder is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\).  On that event the rank-\(d\) SVD projector is the column-space projector of \(\widehat C\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat Q-Q_A
 =-Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+
  -\{Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+\}^\top
  +o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}) \tag{15}
\]
uniformly over \(\Theta\).

The established cumulant-cancellation lemma applies to every \(\theta_n\in\Theta\) and gives
\[
 h_k=m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A=\operatorname{col}(C),
 \qquad Q_Ah_k=0. \tag{16}
\]
It follows directly that
\[
 \{Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+\}^\top h_k
 =C^{+\top}(\widehat C-C)^\top Q_Ah_k=0. \tag{17}
\]
Writing \(\widehat h_k=\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k\), equations (9), (12), and (15)--(17) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q\widehat h_k
 &=\sqrt n\,Q_A(\widehat h_k-h_k)
   +\sqrt n(\widehat Q-Q_A)h_k
   +\sqrt n(\widehat Q-Q_A)(\widehat h_k-h_k)\\
 &=\sqrt n\,Q_A\{(\widehat m_k-m_k)
       -\beta(\widehat c_k-c_k)\}
   -\sqrt n\,Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+h_k+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \end{aligned} \tag{18}
\]
Indeed, the product in the first line is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) after multiplication by \(\sqrt n\), uniformly.  Substitution of (9) into (18) proves
\[
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{\mathbb P}(1), \tag{19}
\]
where
\[
 \zeta_{e,k,n}
 =Q_A\{\psi^m_{e,k,n}-\beta\psi^c_{e,k,n}
       -\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\}. \tag{20}
\]
The finite number of \(k\)'s makes the remainders simultaneous.  Formula (20) proves the asserted estimated-plane correction, including its sign.

It remains to establish the Gaussian approximation without a covariance-rank condition.  Stack (20) over \(d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\).  Equations (11), (12), and the uniform bounds on \(h_k\) imply
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta_n}\mathbb E_{\theta_n}\|\zeta_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}<\infty. \tag{21}
\]
For \(a=(e,i)\), put
\[
 X_a=n^{-1/2}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}),
 \qquad L_n=\sum_a\mathbb E\|X_a\|^{2+\nu}.
\]
Then (1) and (21) give
\[
 L_n\leq K n^{-1-\nu/2}\sum_e n_e\pi_e^{-(2+\nu)}
 \leq K'n^{-\nu/2}. \tag{22}
\]
For each \(a\), let \(G_a\) be an independent centered Gaussian vector with the same covariance as \(X_a\).  Fixed-dimensional Gaussian integration and Lyapunov's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E\|G_a\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K\{\mathbb E\|X_a\|^2\}^{1+\nu/2}
 \leq K\mathbb E\|X_a\|^{2+\nu}. \tag{23}
\]
To verify the replacement rather than invoke a nonsingular limit theorem, let \(f\) be bounded by one and one-Lipschitz, and convolve it with \(N(0,\varepsilon^2I)\) to obtain \(f_\varepsilon\).  Differentiation under the Gaussian integral gives
\[
 \sup_x\|D^2f_\varepsilon(x)\|\leq K\varepsilon^{-1},
 \qquad
 \sup_x\|D^3f_\varepsilon(x)\|\leq K\varepsilon^{-2}.
\]
Interpolating these two bounds yields
\[
 \|D^2f_\varepsilon(x)-D^2f_\varepsilon(y)\|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}\|x-y\|^\nu. \tag{24}
\]
The integral Taylor remainder is consequently bounded by
\[
 \left|f_\varepsilon(x+v)-f_\varepsilon(x)-Df_\varepsilon(x)v
 -\tfrac12v^\top D^2f_\varepsilon(x)v\right|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}\|v\|^{2+\nu}. \tag{25}
\]
Replacing the \(X_a\)'s successively by the \(G_a\)'s cancels the constant, linear, and quadratic expectations because each pair has equal mass, mean, and covariance.  Equations (23)--(25) therefore give
\[
 \left|\mathbb Ef_\varepsilon\!\left(\sum_aX_a\right)
 -\mathbb Ef_\varepsilon\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)\right|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}L_n. \tag{26}
\]
Translation coupling also gives \(\|f_\varepsilon-f\|_\infty\leq K\varepsilon\).  Choosing \(\varepsilon=L_n^{1/(2+\nu)}\) when \(L_n>0\), and observing that both sums vanish almost surely when \(L_n=0\), proves from (22)--(26) that
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\!\left(\sum_aX_a\right),
 \mathcal L\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)\right)\longrightarrow0 \tag{27}
\]
uniformly.  Finally, stratified independence and \(n_e=n\pi_e\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)
 =\frac1n\sum_e n_e\pi_e^{-2}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^\top]
 =\Sigma_n. \tag{28}
\]
Thus the Gaussian sum has law \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\).  The construction is valid for every positive semidefinite \(\Sigma_n\); if it is singular, this Gaussian is supported on its image, and if it is zero, it is the point mass at zero.  Equations (19), (27), and (28) prove the lemma.  No step used \(r\), \(\lambda_n\), a nonzero projected contrast, or a breakout condition.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\},
 \qquad
 \varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}=\frac{\nu}{8+4\nu}.
\]
Let \(0<\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\) and \(m_n\to\infty\) be deterministic.  The randomized-jitter Gaussian-multiplier set \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\) is implementable from the stratified observations and auxiliary standard normal draws.  Uniformly over the bounded ambient class \(\Theta\), including its no-breakout members,
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)
 \right|=0,
\]
where the probability is unconditional over the observations, all Gaussian multipliers, the observed-statistic jitter, and all Monte Carlo jitters.  The conclusion allows the same-sample estimated-\(A\) influence covariance \(\Sigma_n\) to be singular, to change rank with \(n\), or to equal zero, and it uses neither a covariance inverse nor a positive-eigenvalue bound.  Since \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\to0\), the randomization vanishes on the root-\(n\) projected-moment scale.  This is exact null calibration of an Anderson--Rubin inversion; no expected-length or diameter optimality is claimed for \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\).

There is a precise atomic limitation for deterministic single-threshold calibration.  If a reference statistic has distribution function \(F\), has an atom at a proposed cutoff \(x_0\), and
\[
 F(x_0-)<1-\alpha_0<F(x_0),
\]
then neither the deterministic rule accepting below \(x_0\) nor the deterministic rule accepting at or below \(x_0\) has acceptance probability \(1-\alpha_0\).  This limitation concerns only those deterministic single-threshold conventions at an atom; it is not an impossibility claim about every procedure without external randomization.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathcal K=\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and use the block maximum norm in the randomized-inversion definition.  Its dimension
\[
 D_{\mathrm{AR}}=(E-1)(R_{\max}-d-1)
\]
is fixed.  All bounds below are uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\).  By balanced shares, \(n_e\geq n\underline\pi\); hence every \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The small-sample fallback is therefore well defined and eventually inactive.

At the true value \(b=\beta\), the ambient generated-projector expansion gives
\[
 H_n(\beta)=Z_n+R_n,
 \qquad
 Z_n=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}), \tag{1}
\]
where \(R_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly and
\[
 \Sigma_n=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\pi_e^{-1}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}]. \tag{2}
\]
Put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\}>0,
 \qquad a=\nu/2.
\]
The construction in that lemma, the source moment envelope, the coefficient bounds, and \(\|C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0^{-1}\) give
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta\in\Theta}
 \mathbb E_\theta\|\zeta_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}\leq K. \tag{3}
\]
The division by \(\sigma_d(C)\) is licensed by the calibration-gap assumption.  No projected treatment contrast is divided by anywhere in this proof.

We first record rates for the observed Gaussian approximation.  Set
\[
 X_{e,i,n}=n^{-1/2}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}).
\]
Balanced shares and (3) imply
\[
 \sum_{e,i}\mathbb E\|X_{e,i,n}\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K n^{-\nu/2}. \tag{4}
\]
For a bounded one-Lipschitz function, Gaussian convolution at bandwidth \(s\), the second-order Taylor formula, and successive replacement by covariance-matched Gaussian summands give, exactly as in equations (24)--(27) of the ambient expansion proof,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\}
 \leq K\{s+n^{-\nu/2}s^{-1-\nu}\}.
\]
Taking \(s=n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}\) yields
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_\theta(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\}
 \leq K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}
 =K n^{-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}. \tag{5}
\]
This calculation uses only covariance matching and therefore permits singular \(\Sigma_n\).

We also need a rate for \(R_n\) because the jitter scale vanishes.  For every canonical projection of order \(j\geq2\), the equal-index-set calculation in the ambient expansion proof gives variance \(O(n_e^{-j})\) before root-\(n\) scaling and hence \(O(n^{-1})\) after that scaling.  The projector remainder on \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|\leq\kappa_0/2\}\) is bounded by \(K\sqrt n\|\widehat C-C\|^2\).  The first-projection representation and (3) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat C-C\|^2\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\|\widehat C-C\|>\kappa_0/2\}\leq K/n. \tag{6}
\]
On the exceptional event we truncate the distance at one.  Cauchy--Schwarz treats every product of two first-order estimation errors in the same way.  Summing the finitely many terms gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta[1\wedge\|R_n\|]
 \leq K n^{-1/2}. \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, adding \(R_n\) in (1) changes expectations of bounded one-Lipschitz functions by at most the left side of (7), and (5)--(7) give
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_\theta(H_n(\beta)),N(0,\Sigma_n)\}
 \leq K n^{-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}. \tag{8}
\]
Here \(2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\leq1/2\), so the term in (7) is no larger in order than the displayed bound.

We next prove the quantitative estimated-influence replacement required for the conditional multiplier law.  For an order-\(s\) constituent kernel \(g\), define its population first projection by
\[
 \psi_{g,e}(w)=s\{\mathbb E[g(w,W_2,\ldots,W_s)]-\mathbb Eg\}.
\]
When \(s\geq2\), conditionally on \(W_{e,i}\), the leave-one-out average in \(\widehat\psi_{g,e,i}\) is an order-\((s-1)\) \(U\)-statistic based on the remaining observations.  In its conditional variance, disjoint tuples are conditionally independent, and there are \(O(n_e^{2s-3})\) overlapping pairs among \(O(n_e^{2s-2})\) ordered pairs.  The kernel second moment is bounded by (5) of the ambient expansion proof.  Thus the conditional-estimation error has unconditional second moment at most \(K/n_e\).  When \(s=1\), that conditional-estimation error is zero.  The same overlap count gives \(\mathbb E|U_{e,s}(g)-\mathbb Eg|^2\leq K/n_e\).  After applying the finitely many linear combinations and contrast signs, we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E R_n^\psi\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 R_n^\psi=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \|\widehat\psi_{e,i}-\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2. \tag{9}
\]
Conditional Jensen's inequality applied to the leave-one-out averages and ordinary Jensen applied to the \(U\)-statistics also give uniform \((2+\nu)\)-moment bounds for both estimated and population first projections, because \((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\).

Put \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\), \(\widehat h_k=\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k\), and
\[
 L_n^2=\|\widehat Q-Q_A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 +\|\widehat C^\dagger-C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 +\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\|\widehat h_k-h_k\|^2. \tag{10}
\]
On \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|\leq\kappa_0/2\}\), the inverse identity and projector expansion give
\(\|\widehat C^\dagger-C^+\|+\|\widehat Q-Q_A\|\leq K\|\widehat C-C\|\).  Off this event, the threshold in the definition gives \(\|\widehat C^\dagger\|\leq2/\kappa_0\), while (6) controls the event.  The same \(U\)-statistic mean-square bounds control \(\widehat h_k-h_k\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E L_n^2\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E L_n\leq K n^{-1/2}. \tag{11}
\]
Define
\[
 Y_n=1+\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \{\|\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2+\|\widehat\psi_{e,i}\|^2\}.
\]
Since \(1+a=1+\nu/2\), Jensen's inequality for the empirical average and the \((2+\nu)\)-moment bounds give
\[
 \mathbb E Y_n^{1+a}\leq K. \tag{12}
\]
Adding and subtracting one factor at a time in the definitions of \(\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)\) and \(\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\), and using the uniform bounds on \(C^+\), \(\widehat C^\dagger\), and \(h_k\), yields the deterministic inequality
\[
 B_n:=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \|\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)-\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2
 \leq K\{R_n^\psi+L_n^2Y_n\}. \tag{13}
\]
No independence between \(L_n\) and \(Y_n\) is used.

Define
\[
 \widetilde\Sigma_n=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})^\top,
\]
and let \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)\) be the analogous empirical matrix formed from \(\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)\); this is exactly the conditional covariance of one multiplier draw.  The inequality
\(\|xx^\top-yy^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\|x-y\|(\|x\|+\|y\|)\), empirical Cauchy--Schwarz, and (13) give
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K\{(R_n^\psi Y_n)^{1/2}+L_nY_n+R_n^\psi+L_n^2Y_n\}. \tag{14}
\]
We integrate (14) explicitly.  For every \(t>0\), (9) and (12) imply
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge R_n^\psi Y_n]
 \leq t\mathbb ER_n^\psi+\Pr(Y_n>t)
 \leq K\{t/n+t^{-(1+a)}\}. \tag{15}
\]
Taking \(t=n^{1/(2+a)}\), followed by Jensen's inequality for the square root, gives
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge(R_n^\psi Y_n)^{1/2}]
 \leq K n^{-\kappa},
 \qquad
 \kappa=\frac{1+a}{2(2+a)}. \tag{16}
\]
Likewise, (11)--(12), without any independence assertion, give
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge L_nY_n]
 \leq t\mathbb EL_n+\Pr(Y_n>t)
 \leq K\{tn^{-1/2}+t^{-(1+a)}\}.
\]
With \(t=n^{1/\{2(2+a)\}}\), this is at most \(Kn^{-\kappa}\).  The same split with \(L_n^2\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge L_n^2Y_n]\leq K n^{-(1+a)/(2+a)},
\]
and (9) controls \(R_n^\psi\).  Therefore (14) implies
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]
 \leq K n^{-\kappa}. \tag{17}
\]

It remains to center the true-influence empirical covariance.  By (3), each matrix \(\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^\top\) has uniformly bounded \((1+a)\)-moment.  Truncate its norm at
\[
 \ell_n=n^{1/\{2(1+a)\}}.
\]
The mean norm of the discarded tail is at most \(K\ell_n^{-a}\).  In fixed dimension, the expected norm of the average of the centered truncated matrices is bounded by its root mean square, which is at most
\[
 K n^{-1/2}\ell_n^{(1-a)/2}
\]
after applying balanced shares.  This is no larger than the tail order.  Since \(\mathbb E\widetilde\Sigma_n=\Sigma_n\), we obtain
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta
 \|\widetilde\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K n^{-a/\{2(1+a)\}}
 =K n^{-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}. \tag{18}
\]
The identities
\[
 2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}=\frac{a}{2(1+a)},
 \qquad
 \kappa-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}
 =\frac{1}{2(2+a)(1+a)}>0 \tag{19}
\]
follow by direct algebra.  Because \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\) with \(\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\), equations (17)--(19) prove the required quantitative replacement:
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]=o(\tau_n^2), \tag{20}
\]
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]=o(\tau_n^2). \tag{21}
\]

Conditionally on the data, \(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\) is exactly Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)\).  For positive semidefinite matrices \(S,T\), the integral representation
\[
 S^{1/2}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2}S(S+tI)^{-1}\,dt
\]
and the resolvent identity, split at \(t=\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), give
\[
 \|S^{1/2}-T^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}. \tag{22}
\]
The derivation does not require positive eigenvalues.  Couple the conditional multiplier Gaussian and \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\) as \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)^{1/2}Z\) and \(\Sigma_n^{1/2}Z\), with \(Z\sim N(0,I_{D_{\mathrm{AR}}})\).  Equations (21)--(22), truncation at distance one, and Jensen's inequality imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L^*(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)),N(0,\Sigma_n)\}
 \leq K n^{-\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}=o(\tau_n). \tag{23}
\]

Now let \(G_n\sim N(0,\Sigma_n)\), let \(\xi\sim N(0,1)\) be independent, and define
\[
 F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)
 =\Pr\{\|G_n\|_{\max}+\tau_n\xi\leq t\}.
\]
For every \(t\), the function
\[
 x\longmapsto
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\|x\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}\right)
\]
is bounded by one and has Lipschitz constant at most \((\sqrt{2\pi}\tau_n)^{-1}\).  Applying (8) and (23), and using \(\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\), yields
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta,t}
 \left|\Pr_\theta\{V_n(\beta)\leq t\}-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)\right|
 \longrightarrow0, \tag{24}
\]
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta\sup_t
 \left|\Pr^*\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\leq t\}-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)\right|
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{25}
\]
Indeed, the bounds are respectively \(O(n^{\chi-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}})\) and \(O(n^{\chi-\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}})\).

The ideal distribution function is continuous and strictly increasing even if \(\Sigma_n\) is singular or zero, because its density is
\[
 t\longmapsto
 \mathbb E\!\left[\tau_n^{-1}\phi\!\left(
 \frac{t-\|G_n\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}\right)\right]>0. \tag{26}
\]
Consequently, if \(V_n^\circ\) has distribution function \(F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}\), then \(1-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(V_n^\circ)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\).  The uniform distribution-function approximation (24) therefore implies
\[
 1-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(V_n(\beta))\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Unif}(0,1)
\]
uniformly over \(\Theta\).  Equation (25) shows, by evaluating the two conditional distribution functions at the random argument \(V_n(\beta)\), that the conditional upper-tail probability
\[
 p_n^*(\beta)=\Pr^*\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\geq V_n(\beta)\}
\]
differs from \(1-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(V_n(\beta))\) by \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly.  The conditional comparison distribution is continuous because of its independent Gaussian jitter, so the weak inequality creates no tie term.  Hence
\[
 p_n^*(\beta)\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Unif}(0,1) \tag{27}
\]
uniformly over \(\Theta\), including when \(\Sigma_n=0\) or changes rank.

Conditionally on the observations and \(\xi_0\), the \(m_n\) indicators defining \(\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability \(p_n^*(\beta)\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
 \widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)\mid\text{observations},\xi_0
 \right)
 =\frac{p_n^*(\beta)\{1-p_n^*(\beta)\}}{m_n}
 \leq\frac1{4m_n}. \tag{28}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_n\to\infty\) show that the Monte Carlo error is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly.  Because \(\alpha_0\in(0,1/2)\) is a continuity point of the uniform distribution, (27)--(28) give
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \left|\Pr_\theta\{\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)>\alpha_0\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)\right|\longrightarrow0. \tag{29}
\]
The event in (29) is exactly \(\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}\).  The probability integrates over the stratified observations, every multiplier, \(\xi_0\), and every Monte Carlo jitter.  This proves the asserted exact unconditional coverage.  Since \(\tau_n\to0\), both observed and multiplier jitters vanish on the root-\(n\) projected-moment scale.  Coverage alone supplies no expected-length or diameter assertion, so none is inferred.

Finally, suppose \(F\) has an atom at \(x_0\).  The deterministic strict single-threshold rule has acceptance probability \(F(x_0-)\), while the deterministic weak rule has acceptance probability \(F(x_0)\).  If
\[
 F(x_0-)<1-\alpha_0<F(x_0),
\]
neither probability equals \(1-\alpha_0\).  This proves exactly the stated limitation.  It does not exclude randomized acceptance on the equality event or other non-threshold procedures.
